BiblicalUsage: gᵉdûwlâh — greatness. That is the whole of it, and it is enough: 11 occurrences, and in 2 Samuel, 1 Chronicles, Esther, and Psalms the meaning never wavers. I keep coming back to the simple reading because the simple reading is the true one.
TheologicalSignificance: What gᵉdûwlâh tells me is that true strength belongs to the Lord, and He lends it to His people. I hold that the simple reading is the true one, and I will not trade it for a clever one.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
